अकर्कर: Akarkara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
अकूपार: Akūpāra m.: A mythical king of tortoises, living in the lake Indradyumna (सरस्) 3. 191. 9, 14. A. Long-lived: Of fabulous age, he recognized king Indradyumna whom even Mārkaṇḍeya (sage), Prākārakarṇa (owl), and Nāḍījaṅgha (crane) could not; king Indradyumna, in bygone days, had placed a thousand times Akūpāra first (उपहित-पूर्वः) while establishing the fire altars (अग्निचिति) 3. 191. 14-18; [for the use of tortoise in Agnicayana cf. Tait. Saṃ. 5. 2. 8. 4-5; ĀpŚrS. 16. 13. 10; 16 25. 1.]. B. Myth: Requested by gods and demons to support mountain Mandara at the time of churning the ocean; Akūpāra agreed, where-upon Indra with his tool fixed the top of mountain Mandara on his back (कूर्मेण तु तथेत्युक्त्वा पृष्ठम् अस्य समर्पितम् । तस्य शैलस्य चाग्रं वै यन्त्रेणेन्द्रो ऽभ्यपीडयत्) 1. 16. 10-11.
अग्रतेजस्: Agratejas m.: A mythical serpent. He, and other serpents, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12. [Agratejas, name of an independent serpent or an epithet of Śitikaṇṭha ?]
अङ्गद: Aṅgada m.: A monkey-chief, son of Vālin 3. 266. 27; 3. 272. 17. A. Qualities: Wise (प्राज्ञ- 3. 267. 54), eloquent (वाग्मी 3. 268. 9), and lustrous (तेजस्वी 3. 268. 22). B. Functions: Sent with Hanūmant and others to the south in search of Sītā; on their way back, rested in the Madhuvana of Vālin (3. 266. 27); he, along with other monkey-chiefs, protected Rāma's army of monkeys on their way to Laṅkā 3. 267. 19; after crossing the ocean Rāma sent him as his envoy (दौत्येन) to Rāvaṇa 3. 267. 54; reaching the gate of Laṅkā he informed Rāvaṇa of his arrival (3. 268. 7), and then conveyed Rāma's message (10-16) to Rāvaṇa; when four Rākṣasas tried to capture him by holding him at his four limbs, he jumped up with them in the sky to reach a terrace; on his return, honoured by Rāma 3. 268. 19, 22. C. Part in war: Helped Lakṣmaṇa in his fight against Indrajit; he struck Indrajit with a tree on his head; Indrajit wanted to hit Aṅgada on his chest with a missile (प्रास) but it was cut off by Lakṣmaṇa; Indrajit struck him on his left side with गदा; enraged, Aṅgada hurled the trunk of a Śāla tree to kill Indrajit, but it struck his chariot and destroyed it together with horses and charioteer 3. 272. 14-18; he was among the monkey-chiefs who surrounded Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa when they lay on the ground bound by the arrows of Indrajit 3. 273. 4; he and the other monkey-chiefs applied water, sent by Kubera, to their eyes which enabled them to see beings who made themselves invisible 3. 273. 13; he, along with others, surrounded Rāvaṇa rushing towards Rāma, and destroyed with trees Rāvaṇa's army 3. 274. 3. D. Reward: Rāma anointed Aṅgada, who had done his duties (कृतकर्माणम्), as crown prince of Kiṣkindhā 3. 275. 57.

Aṅgada m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada in the south. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (अथा-परे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56; (कुकु-राङ्गदमारिषाः) 6. 10. 59.
अञ्जन: Añjana m.: A mythical elephant, living in the पाताल 5. 97. 1. One of the best elephants (वारणसत्तम) born in the family of Supratīka 5. 97. 15; one of the दिङ्नागस् on whom rode the Rākṣasas accompanying Ghaṭotkaca against Bhagadatta 6. 60. 51; elephants born in his family known as Añjanakas 7. 87. 33, 16.
Añjana m.: Name of a mountain. Yudhiṣṭhira was instructed by the great sage Asita near the mountain Añjana (अश्रौ-षीर् असितस्यापि महर्षेर् अञ्जनं प्रति) 2. 69. 13. [See Añjanābha]
अतिषण्ड: Atiṣaṇḍa m.: A mythical serpent. He, and other serpents, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12.
अनघ: Anagha m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 12, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked by श्रीवत्स; his deity Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because engaged in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
अनन्त: Ananta m.: A mythical serpent. A. Birth: A काद्रवेय, son of Kadrū (daughter of Dakṣa) 1. 59. 40. B. Des-cription: Of great strength (वीर्यवान्, महाबलः) 1. 16. 6-7, of great prowess (प्रतापवान्) 1. 32. 24, of great expanse (विभुः) 1. 32. 24; divine (भगवान् देवः) 18. 5. 20. C. Feats: He uprooted, at the instance of Brahman and Nārāyaṇa, mount Mandara for churning the ocean 1. 16. 6-7; when the ocean was being churned, he stood by the side of Nārāyaṇa and raised up and put down again and again the head of Vāsuki (used as a churning rope) 1. 16. 14; (identified with Śeṣa 6. 63 10) he dwells below the earth and holds it on his head at the instance of Brahman 1 32. 24; supports the earth by योग 18. 5. 20; Brahman gave him Suparṇa, the son of Vinatā, as friend 1. 32. 25. D. Great-ness: As the best among the serpents he is one of the विभूतिस् of Bhagavān 6. 32. 29; Śiva praised as ‘Ananta among the Nāgas’ 13. 14. 158. E. Upamāna: The peak of mount Meru compared with Ananta 13. 15. 9; huge shape, similar to that of Ananta, was assumed by Irāvān to attack Alambusa 6. 86. 67. F. End: (As Balarāma) having accomplished his functions he entered the रसातल 18. 5. 20 (cf. 16. 5. 12-13). [See Śeṣa].
अनल: Anala m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; living on serpents; marked by श्रीवत्स; his deity Viṣṇu; by actions a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because engaged in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
अनिल: Anila m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked by श्रीवत्स; his deity Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because engaged in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
अनील: Anīla m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.
अन्ध: Andha m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Puri 5. 101. 16, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
अपराजित: Aparājita m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 15, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also mentioned by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 13.
अम्बरीष: Ambarīṣa m.: A mythical serpent. He, among others, received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12.
अरिष्टनेमि: Ariṣṭanemi m.: A mythical bird. Son of Vinatā (daughter of Dakṣa) 1. 59. 39; came with Tārkṣya and others to greet Arjuna at his birth 1. 114. 62, 40.
अरुण: Aruṇa m.: A mythical bird. A. Birth: Not fully developed (विकल) son of Vinatā and Kaśyapa 1. 27. 34, 25; one of the six Vainateyas 1. 59. 39; 1. 114. 62; Vinatā, wife of Kaśyapa, broke open one of her two eggs prematurely after waiting for five hundred years; when Aruṇa, her son, came out he was developed only in his forepart; for her impatience he cursed Vinatā to be the slave of Kadrū for five hundred years, and also told her that her second son will free her from slavery, if she did not break open the other egg before the proper time arrived; he then left his mother and flew into the sky; he now appears as Aruṇa (red light) at dawn 1. 14. 12-21; 1. 31. 1; hence called the fore-runner of the sun (आदित्यस्य पुरःसरः) 1. 27. 34; 7. 161. 2. B. Wife and Children: His wife Śyenī bore him two sons, Sampāti and Jaṭāyu(s) 1. 60. 67; hence Jaṭāyu called अरुणात्मज 3. 263. 1. C. Importance: Kaśyapa blessed his wife with two sons who would be lords of the three worlds (त्रिभुवनेश्वरौ), hon-oured by all worlds (लोकपूजितौ), of great fortune (महाभागौ) 1. 27. 26-27; destined to be an ally of Indra 1. 27. 30; present at Skanda's consecration as सेनापति 9. 44. 14; came with other Vainateyas to greet Arjuna at his birth 1. 114. 62; counted among the Ādityas 1. 60. 38; he gave Skanda a cock having a red-crest (ताम्रचूड) and fighting with nails (चरणायुध) 9. 45. 46. D. Upamāna: Ghaṭotkaca with his charioteer Virūpākṣa compared with Sun and Aruṇa 7. 150. 14; Karṇa with Śalya to work together as do Sun and Aruṇa 8. 23. 15.
अरुणात्मज: Aruṇātmaja m.: Son of Aruṇa, Jaṭāyu 3. 263. 1.
अरुणानुज: Aruṇānuja m.: Younger brother of Aruṇa, Garuḍa 5. 110. 3.
अर्बुद: Arbuda m.: A mythical serpent. Lived near the town Girivraja, in Mag-adha; described as ‘tormenter of enemies’ (शत्रुतापन) 2. 19. 9.

Arbuda m.: Name of a mountain. Described as the ‘son of Himavant’ (हिमवत्सुतम् अर्बुदम्); the mountain stands now, where formerly there was a hole in the earth (पृथिव्यां यत्र वै छिद्रं पूर्वम् आसीद् युधिष्ठिर) 3. 80. 74; on this mountain there is the world famous आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha; by living there for a night one obtained the fruit of donating a thousand cows (गोसहस्रफलम्) 3. 80. 75.
अलर्क: Alarka m.: A worm (कृमि). Feeding on flesh and blood (मांसशोणित-भोजन), covered with phlegm (श्लेष्म-मय), harsh to touch (दारुणस्पर्श); looked like a boar; had eight legs, sharp jaws, covered with hair sharp as needles 12. 3. 13, 6-7, 12-13; it bit and cut open Karṇa's thigh 12. 3. 7-8; really a great Asura, Gṛtsa by name, who was born as a worm due to the curse of Bhṛgu 12. 3. 14-20.
अश्वक्रन्द: Aśvakranda m.: A mythical bird (?) Tore open by Garuḍa with nails and beak during his expedition to fetch अमृत 1. 28. 18, 20. [Name of a Yakṣa according to Nila-kaṇṭha].
अश्वतर: Aśvatara m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. A. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7. B. Men-tioned among serpents who wait, without fatigue (विगतक्लम), on Varuṇa in his सभा 2. 9. 9; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फण-वन्त्) 2. 9. 10. C. Also listed among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 10.

Aśvatara nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near Prayāga; together with Prayāga, Pratiṣṭhāna, Kambala and Bhogavatī it is considered to be the altar of Prajāpati (वेदी प्रोक्ता प्रजापतेः) 3. 83. 72; there the Vedas and the sacrifices in bodily form, as well as the sages, wait upon Prajāpati, and the gods and the Cakracaras offer sacrifices 3. 83. 73.
अश्वत्थामन्: Aśvatthāman m.: Name of a famous elephant. In the army of Indravarman, king of Mālava, who was fighting from the side of the Pāṇḍavas; as tall as a mountain; could be compared with the elephant of Indra; Bhīma killed him to proclaim “Aśvatthāman is dead” 7. 164. 71, 73, 101, 102; 7. 165. 113, 115, 116 (also cf. 7. 165. 28-33); Yudhi-ṣṭhira told Droṇa इन्दिस्तिन्च्त्ल्य् (अव्यक्तम्) “Aśvatthāman, the elephant, is killed” 7. 165. 115; 7. 164. 106; but cf. 12. 27. 16-17 (कुञ्जरं चान्तरं कृत्वा मिथ्योपचरितं मया । … मयोक्तो गुरुर् आहवे॑अश्वत्थामा हत इति कुञ्जरे विनिपालिते । ).
अश्वराज: Aśvarāja m.: Name of a horse (?), of a demon (?). Killed by Kṛṣṇa in his childhood 5. 128. 46.
अश्वसेन: Aśvasena m.: A mythical serpent. A. Family and Residence: Takṣaka's son and his constant companion (नित्यं सह-चराव् उभौ) 1. 3. 145; 1. 218. 5; 8. 65. 39; Uttaṅka mentions him, (while praising the नागस्), as one living at Kurukṣetra along the river Ikṣumatī 1. 3. 145. B. Khāṇḍava fire: He was at the Khāṇḍava forest at the time of the great fire, but escaped death 1. 219. 40; his mother swallowed him, head first, so that when Arjuna cut off her head while she was flying upwards Aśvasena did not die 1. 218. 5, 1. 220. 2; Aśvasena could escape because Indra confounded Arjuna with वातवर्ष (an अस्त्र ?) 1. 218. 9. C. Part in the great war: Karṇa had a fiery arrow described as भुजग (8. 66. 10), सर्पमुख (8. 66. 5), poisonous (8. 66. 6, 16); reserved by him for use against Arjuna 8. 66. 5; when the arrow was shot it could remove only Arjuna's diadem (किरीट) 8. 66. 11, 12, 15, 17; on this arrow apparently lay the big snake (महोरग) Aśvasena, inimical to Arjuna due to the killing of his mother by Arjuna 8. 66. 20, 21; Arjuna killed him when Kṛṣṇa explained to him who the serpent really was 8. 66. 21, 24; Aśvasena not directly named in this incident, but Duryo-dhana names him as figuring in this incident when he mentions Aśvasena (as an arrow shot at Arjuna) who was deflected (व्यं-सनेनाश्वसेनस्य) by Kṛṣṇa 9. 60. 35.
अक्षिसंतर्जन: Akṣisaṃtarjana nt.: Name of a missile (अस्त्र). One of the eight missiles known to Arjuna; enumerated by Rāma Jāmadagnya to Duryodhana; when struck by any one of these eight missiles the victim died, or became insane, or lost consciousness, or he slept, or jumped up, vomited, passed urine, or he wept or laughed incessantly; (of these different effects, perhaps Akṣisaṃtarjana only induced the victim to go to sleep ?) 5. 94. 38-40.
अनन्तविजय: Anantavijaya m.: Name of a conch. The conch of Yudhiṣṭhira; he blew it on the first day at the start of the war 6. 23. 16; also the next day 6. 47. 26 (and probably every day thereafter); identical with Vāruṇa Śaṅkha ? [See Vāruṇa (Śaṅkha)].
अन्तकदण्ड: Antakadaṇḍa m.: Weapon of Antaka. [See Daṇḍa].
अन्तर्धान: Antardhāna1 nt.: Name of a missile received by Arjuna from Droṇa. While displaying his skill in the use of the missiles taught to him by Droṇa (आचार्याद् अस्त्रलाघवम् 1. 125. 18), Arjuna made himself invisible by employing this missile (अन्तर्धानेन चास्त्रेण पुनर् अन्तर्हितो ऽभवत्) 1. 125. 20.

Antardhāna2 nt.: Name of a missile received by Arjuna from Kubera. Arjuna received this dear (प्रिय) missile of Kubera with due rites (विधिवत्); hence this heavenly (दिव्य) missile called कौबेर अस्त्र; when used, it deprived the enemy of his vigour, lustre and splendour and sent him to sleep (ओजस्तेजोद्युतिहरं प्रस्वापनम्) 3. 42. 33-34.
अयोजाल: Ayojāla nt.: A kind of a missile. Employed by Arjuna while fighting with Kirāta (Śiva); (so called because it produced net of iron ?) 3. 163. 32.
अर्धचन्द्र: Ardhacandra m.: Name of a व्यूह, or महाव्यूह 6. 52. 10; 6. 52. 18; 8. 7. 32. (1) On the third day of the war Arjuna, in consultation with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, made use of this व्यूह to counter the Garuḍa-vyūha of the Kauravas (6. 52. 2); Bhīma-sena, surrounded by different kings, formed the right horn (दक्षिण शृङ्ग) of थे व्यूह; behind him stood Virāṭa and Drupada, follo-wed by Nīla; behind Nīla was stationed Dhṛṣṭaketu, surrounded by the Cedis, the Kāśis, the Karūṣas and the Pauravas; in the middle of the व्यूह stood Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍin, the Pāñcālas, and the Prabhadrakas, ready to fight; Dharmarāja, surrounded by the army of the elephants also stood there; so also Sātyaki and the five sons of Drau-padī; they were immediately followed by Abhimanyu and Irāvant; then came Ghaṭo-tkaca, the son of Bhīmasena, and the great warriors Kekayas; on the left side of the व्यूह stood Arjuna protected by Janārdana 6. 52. 10-18. (2) On the fifteenth day of the war, Arjuna arranged the Pāṇḍava army according to the Ardhacandravyūha (8. 7. 27) to counter the Makaravyūha (8. 7. 14) of the Kaurava army arranged by Karṇa; Bhīma was stationed on the left, Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna on the right side; in the middle stood Arjuna; Nakula, Sahadeva and Dharmarāja were posted at the back; Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, the two Pāñcāla heroes, acted as the wheel-protectors of Arjuna; the rest of the kings took positions in keeping with their dispositions, energy and mettle (यथा-भावं यथोत्साहं यथासत्त्वं च) 8. 7. 28-32; viewing this arrangement Yudhiṣṭhira felt confident of victory 8. 7. 34. [See Candrārdha].
अश्मवर्ष: Aśmavarṣa nt.: A kind of a missile. Employed by Arjuna against Kirāta (Śiva); (it produced a hail of stones ?) 3. 163. 32.
अंशावतरण: Aṃśāvataraṇa nt.: Name of a section of the Ādiparvan describing the incarnations of portions of gods (त्वयैवांशावतरणे देवभागाः प्रकीर्तिताः) 1. 109. 3. A part of the Saṃbhavaparvan where partial descent of gods is described (सं-भवपर्वणि … अंशावतरणं चात्र देवा-नां परिकीर्तितम्) 1. 2. 75-76; Brahman asked the gods, the Gandharvas, and the Apsarases to be partially born separately among men in order to lessen the burden of the earth (अस्या भूमेर् निरसितुं भारं भागैः पृथक् पृथक् । अस्याम् एव प्रसूय-ध्वम् … स्वैर् अंशैः संप्रसूयध्वम् यथेष्टं मानुषेष्व् इति) 1. 58. 46-47; Indra then requested Nārāyaṇa (Hari) to be partially born, to which request he agreed (अंशेनावतरस्वेति तथेत्याह च तं हरिः) 1. 58. 51; Nārada, seeing the kings who had assembled for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira, remembered the conversation which in the bygone days took place (पुरावृत्तां कथाम्) in the residence of Brahman in regard to the partial incar-nations on the earth and recognized that what he saw before him was in fact the assembly of the gods (देवानां संगमम्) 2. 33. 11-13; at the request of Janamejaya, Vaiśayṃpāyana narrated to him the incarna-tions of the Dānavas and the gods 1. 61. 1-2; this is the narration of Aṃśāvataraṇa 1. 61. 99; one is advised to listen to the recitation of the Aṃśāvataraṇa since it brought to the listener wealth, fame, sons, long life and victory; one who listened to the recitation did not perish in adverse circumstances 1. 61. 101-102.
अघमर्षण: Aghamarṣaṇa nt.: Name of a sacred text (Ṛgveda 10. 190. 1-3) composed by the sage Aghamarṣaṇa, son of Madhucchandas. According to Manu, one who takes a dip into water and recites the Aghamarṣaṇa मन्त्रस् thrice (a day) acquires the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice; such a person drives away quickly his sin, is honoured, and all beings try to please him (अपि चैनं प्रसी-दन्ति भूतानि) 12. 148. 26-27; one who bathes in the water of the Kulyātīrtha and repeats the Aghamarṣaṇa मन्त्रस् and, remaining undefiled, fasts for three nights gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice 13. 26. 53; while observing the ब्रह्मचर्य vow, if one slips (makes a fault) in sleep he should recite mentally the Aghamarṣaṇa मन्त्रस् thrice; this way he burns the sin within himself which was the result of the quality of passion (मग्नः स्वप्ने च मनसा त्रिर् जपेद् अघमर्षणम् ॥ पाप्मानं निर्दहेद् एवम् अन्तर्भूतं रजोमयम्) 12. 207. 13-14.
अथर्वन्: Atharvan (sg., pl.), Atharvaṇa, Atharvaveda, Atharvāṇa m.: Name of one of the four vedas; मन्त्रस् of this Veda. A. Origin: The god of gods (Nārā-yaṇa) told Mārkaṇḍeya that the three Vedas and the Atharvaṇa arise out of him and enter into him again (यजुर्वेदो ऽप्यथर्-वणः । मत्तः प्रादुर्भवन्त्य् एते माम् एव प्रविशन्ति च) 3. 187. 14. B. What it does and does not contain: Vyāsa told his son Śuka that one should study the त्रयी विद्या contained in the Ṛk, the Yajus, and the Sāman, as also in the Atharvan (त्रयीविद्याम् अवेक्षेत वेदेषूक्ताम् अथाङ्ग-तः । ऋक्सामवर्णाक्षरतो यजुषोऽथर्वणस् तथा) 12. 227. 1; Bhagavān (Kṛṣṇa) told Arjuna that the great sages had mentioned many of his names in the Atharvan as well as in the other vedas (ऋग्वेदे सयजुर्वेदे तथैवाथर्वसामसु … बहूनि मम नामानि कीर्तितानि महर्षिभिः) 12. 328. 8-9; the sage Sanatsujāta told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the highest principle (ब्रह्मन्) was not to be found in the Atharvan मन्त्रस्, nor in the ऋक्स्, the यजुस्, or the सामन्स् (नैवर्क्षु तन् न यजुःषु नाप्य् अथर्वसु न चैव दृश्यत्य् अमलेषु सामसु) 5. 44. 21. C. Object of study: Sages versed in the Atha-rvaveda recited this Saṃhitā in accordance with the पद and the क्रम mode of recitation (अथर्ववेदप्रवराः … संहि-ताम् ईरयन्ति स्म पदक्रमयुतां तु ते) 1. 64. 33; a certain Ṛṣi, born in the family of a Purohita (not named), when grew up learnt, among other sciences, the Veda and the Atharvaveda (अथर्ववेदे वेदे च बभूवर्षिः सुनिश्चितः) 13. 10. 34; Bhaga-vān (Kṛṣṇa) told Arjuna that the Vipras who had learnt the Atharvāṇa looked upon him as Atharvan consisting of five कल्पस्, enlarged by कृत्यास् (पञ्चकल्पम् अथर्वा-णं कृत्याभिः परिबृंहितम् । कल्पयन्ति हि मां विप्रा अथर्वाणविदस् तथा) 12. 330. 34. D. Use: 1. For worship: When the sage Aṅgiras visited Indra he used for worshipping the god the मन्त्रस् from the Atharvaveda (अथर्ववेदमन्त्रैश् च); Indra, while giving the sage a boon addressed him as Atharvāṅgiras and said that the मन्त्रस् from the Atharvaveda used by him for his praise would be known as the Atharvāṅgirasa section of that Veda (अथर्वाङ्गिरसं नाम अस्मिन् वेदे भ-विष्यति । उदाहरणम् एतद् धि) 5. 18. 5-7; 2. For magic: the Daityas and the Dānavas residing in the Pātāla and who had studied the different मन्त्रस् performed a sacrificial rite (कर्म वैतानसंभवम्) by using मन्त्रस् which included those known from the Atharvaveda (बृहस्पत्युशनोक्तैश् च मन्त्रैर् मन्त्रविशारदाः । अथर्ववेद-प्रोक्तैश् च) in order to produce a कृत्या who was commissioned to fetch Duryodhana who had decided to fast unto death 3. 239. 20. E. Personified: the Atharvaveda, along with the other three Vedas, seen by Nārada in the Sabhā of god Brahmadeva (अथर्ववेदश् च तथा … सर्वं तस्यां मया दृष्टम्) 2. 11. 23, 33, [See Atharvaśiras, Atharvāṅgi-rasa, Ātharvaṇa]
अथर्वशिरस्: Atharvaśiras nt.: Name of an Upaniṣad ? A Brahmacārī who had observed the vows (यतव्रत) and who had studied the Atharvaśiras (अथर्वतिरसोऽध्येता) was to be looked upon as respectable (पङ्क्तिपावन ‘who purifies those who sit along with him in a line to take food’) 13. 90. 22 [cf. य इदम् अथर्वशिरो ब्राह्मणोऽधीते अश्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियो भवति section 7 of the Atharva-śiras Upaniṣad]; A Brāhmaṇa taught Kuntī a group of मन्त्रस् which were revealed in the Atharvaśiras (ततस् ताम् अनवद्याङ्गीम् ग्राहयाम् आस वै द्विजः । मन्त्रग्रामं तदा राजन्न् अथर्वशिरसि श्रुतं); whichever deity Kuntī chose to invite with one of the मन्त्रस् from this मन्त्रग्राम was sure to arrive and be under her control 3. 289. 20. [See Atharvan, Atharvāṅgirasa, Ātharvaṇa]
अथर्वाङ्गिरस: Atharvāṅgirasa m. nt. (sg., pl.), Atharvāṅgīrasī f.: Name of one of the four Vedas, or of an extract from that Veda. Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) told the seven sages (Marīci, Atri and others 12. 322. 27) that the शास्त्र composed by them in a hundred thousand श्लोकस् and from which the धर्म proceeds is one which is approved by (i. e. is in accordance with) the Ṛks, Yajus and Sāmans, as also the Atharvāṅgi-rasas (कृतं शतसहस्रं हि श्लोकानाम् इदम् उत्तमम् । … यस्माद् धर्मः प्रवर्तते ॥ … ऋग्यजुःसामभिर् जुष्टम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसैस् तथा) 12. 322. 36-37; when Kṛṣṇa asked Arjuna to insult Yudhiṣṭhira which was as good as ‘killing’ him, he told Arjuna that his instruction was according to the Atharvāṅgirasī Śruti which was the best among the Śrutis and which should be practised without hesitation by those who desired welfare (अथर्वाङ्गिरसी ह्य् एषा श्रुतीनाम् उत्तमा श्रुतिः । अविचार्यैव कार्यैषा श्रेयःकामैर् नरैः सदा ॥ ) 8. 49. 69; an extract (उदाहरणम्) from the Atharvaveda used by the sage Aṅgiras (or Atharvāṅgiras 5. 18. 6, 8) to praise Indra was to be known as Atharvāṅgirasa (अथर्वाङ्-गिरसं नाम अस्मिन् वेदे भविष्यति । उदाहरणम् एतद् धि) 5. 18. 5-7; the Śakti hurled by Yudhiṣṭhira at Śalya is compared with the कृत्या produced by the मन्त्रस् from the Atharvāṅgirasa (कृत्याम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसीम् इवोग्राम्) 9. 16. 43. [See Atharvan, Atharvaśiras, Ātharvaṇa]
अनुक्रमणी: Anukramaṇī (-ṇi m. c.), Parvānu-kramaṇī f.: Name of the first अध्याय (अनुक्रमणिम् अध्यायम् 1. 1. 62, 199) or पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (भारत-स्त्येतिहासस्य श्रूयतां पर्वसंग्रहः । पर्वानुक्रमणी पूर्वम्) 1. 2. 33-34, 70. In this अध्याय the sage (Vyāsa) is supposed to have made a summary of his Bhārata listing the पर्वन्स् and their (main) events in one hundred and fifty stanzas (ततो ऽध्यर्धशतं ब्यूयः संक्षेपं कृतवान् ऋषिः । अनुक्रमणिम् अध्यायं वृत्तान्तानां सपर्वणाम्) 1. 1. 62; [actually the first अध्याय does not list the पर्वन्स्, which is done in the second अध्याय, but gives an outline of the contents of the epic from the conquests of Pāṇḍu to the end of the war in श्लोकस् 65-158]; one who is faithful (श्रद्दधानः), always striving, and truth-ful and honours this अध्याय (not named here) is freed from sin; one who always hears this Anukramaṇi Adhyāya (अनुक्र-मणिम् अध्यायम्) from the beginning with faith (आस्तिकः) never perishes in adverse circumstances; one who recites some portion of Anukramaṇī at both the twilights is freed from the guilt accumulated during the day and the night 1. 1. 198-200; if one who is pure recites this Adhyāya (not named) on every पर्वन् day he has as good as recited the whole of the Bhārata; one who with faith constantly listens to this अध्याय (not named) declared by the Ṛṣi (आर्षम्) shall obtain long life, fame and heaven 1. 1. 206-207.
अनुगीता: Anugītā f.: Name of the 92nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha. It explains matters related to the knowledge of the soul (अनुगीता ततः पर्व ज्ञेयम् अध्यात्म-वाचकम्) 1. 2. 66, 33, 70. Related to Adhyāyas 14. 16-50 (some of the Adhyāyas are also called Brāhmaṇagītā or Guruśiṣyasaṃvāda).
अनुद्यूत: Anudyūta nt.: Name of the 28th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 41, 33, 70. Referred to in the contents of the Sabhā-pavan 1. 2. 102; related to Adhyāyas 2. 66-72.
अनुशासन: Anuśāsana, Ānuśāsana (1. 2. 201) nt.: Name of the 13th पर्वन् of the Bhārata (1. 2. 201, 204-205) among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् 1. 2. 71. According to the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan it has 146 chapters (अध्यायस्) and 6700 stanzas (श्लोकस्) 1. 2. 205; it is described as the best (उत्तम) 1. 2. 201, and having many topics (सुबहुवृत्तान्त); considered to be the best instruction (उत्तमं चानुशा-सनम्) 1. 2. 204, leading to firm decisions in matters of धर्म (धर्मनिश्च-यकारक) 1. 2. 205; Yudhiṣṭhira, having heard from Bhīṣma in this पर्वन् his deci-sions on धर्म, regained composure (यत्र प्रकृतिम् आपन्नः श्रुत्वा धर्मविनिश्च-यम्) 1. 2. 201; here the matters related to धर्म and अर्थ are fully described, as also the fruits of different gifts, the nature of those who deserve gifts, and the rules of giving gifts; it deals with what is (good) conduct and what one ultimately achieves by observing truth 1. 2. 202-203; in this पर्वन् is narrated also the attainment of heaven by Bhīṣma 1. 2. 204. [See Ānuśāsanika]
अभय: Abhaya m. Name of a dialogue (संवाद) (संवादम् अभयं नाम नामतः) that took place between a Brāh-maṇa who was versed in ज्ञान and विज्ञान and his wife Brāhmaṇī. Called इतिहासम् पुरातनम् 14. 20. 1; the dialogue started when the Brāhmaṇī asked the Brāhmaṇa which world she would go to (after death) having obtained him for husband (14. 20. 4); in this dialogue the Brāhmaṇa stands for mind (मनस्) and the Brāhmaṇī for understanding (बुद्धि) of Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) 14. 34. 12; this संवाद was narrated by Vāsudeva to Pārtha (Arjuna); it comprises अध्यायस् 14. 20-34.
अभिमन्युवध: Abhimanyuvadha m.: Name of the 67th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 57, 33, 70; mentioned in the narration of the contents of the Droṇaparvan 1. 2. 162; also in the summary of the epic 1. 1. 132-134; related to Adhyāyas 7. 32-51.
अम्बोपाख्यान: Ambopākhyāna nt.: Name of the 59th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 54, 33, 70; listed as one of the topics of the Udyogaparvan 1. 2. 150; it comprises Adhyāyas 5. 170-197.
अर्घाभिहरण: Arghābhiharaṇa nt.: Name of the 25th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 41, 33, 70; alluded to as अर्घसंवाद in the narration of the contents of the Sabhāparvan 1. 2. 99; it comprises Adhyāyas 2. 33-36.
अर्जुनस्य: Arjunasya vane vāsaḥ m.: Name of the 17th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 38, 33, 70; alluded to as पार्थस्य वन-वासः in the contents of the Ādiparvan 1. 2. 91; it comprises Adhyāyas 1. 205-210.
अश्मगीत: Aśmagīta nt.: Name of an ancient Itihāsa 12. 28. 2. In this Itihāsa, the Brāhmaṇa Aśman, when questioned by king Janaka of Videha who was overcome by grief how one should face the acquisition and loss of relatives and wealth, instructed him 12. 28. 2-57.
अश्वमेधिक: Aśvamedhika nt.: (1) Name of the 91st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 66, 33, 70; described as ‘the one that destroys all sins’ (सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्) 1. 2. 66; (2) Aśvamedhika (Āśvamedhika 1. 2. 210) nt.: Name of the fourteenth पर्वन् among the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 206; 1. 2. 71; according to the Parvasaṃ-grahaparvan it has 133 chapters (अध्यायस्) and 3320 stanzas (श्लोकस्) as counted by (Vyāsa) who sees the truth (संख्यातास् तत्त्वदर्शिना) 1. 2. 210-211; described as highly wonderful (महाद्भुत) 1. 2. 210; this पर्वन् contains the following topics: the excellent narrative of Saṃvarta and Marutta; the acquisition of gold treasures (by the Pāṇḍavas); the birth of Parikṣit; Parikṣit, who was burnt by the fire of the missile, brought back to life by Kṛṣṇa; the horse (of the Aśvamedha sacrifice) set free for wanderings; Arjuna who followed the horse fought various battles with enraged princes; Arjuna's life in danger in his battle with Babhruvāhana, son of Citrāṅgadā; the story narrated by the mongoose at the Aśvamedha sacrifice 1. 2. 206-209.
अष्टावक्रीय: Aṣṭāvakrīya nt.: Name of an आख्यान listed in the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 120. Here is told how the sage Aṣṭāvakra in a contest (विवाद) defeated Bandin and brought back his father who was plunged into the ocean water 1. 2. 120; comprises Adhyāyas 3. 132-134.
असित: Asita m.: Name of a मन्त्र (?) (of a sage ?) One who remembers the Asita मन्त्र along with the Ārtimant and the Sunītha has no fear from serpents by day or at night 1. 53. 23 (असितं चार्तिमन्तं च सुनीथं चापि यः स्मरेत् । दिवा वा यदि वा रात्रौ नास्य सर्पभयं भवेत् ॥ Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 58. 23 says: प्रसङ्गात् सर्पभयनिवर्तकान् मन्त्रान् पठति । असितम् इत्यादीन्). [See Ārtimant and Sunītha].
Asita m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the west (3. 87. 1); des-cribed as having many roots and fruit (बहुमूलफल) 3. 87. 9.
अङ्गारक: Aṅgāraka m.: Name of the planet Mars; also called Bhauma (13. 151. 12), Lohitāṅga (6. 3. 17; 7. 141. 12). Described as great (महाग्रह) 6. 3. 13; having the lustre of fire (पावकप्रभ) 6. 3. 17; having bright rays (दीप्तरश्मि) 7. 141. 12; Nārada saw Aṅgāraka, along with other Grahas, in the Sabhā of Brahma-deva 2. 11. 20; listed (Bhauma) with other Grahas in the Daivataṃśa 13. 151. 12; by bathing in Mahāgaṅgā at the conjunction of Mars with the Kṛttikās (कृत्तिकाङ्गारके) and by fasting for a fortnight one is purified and obtains heaven 13. 26. 20; Aṅgāraka figures in similes and bad omens: 1. Similes: Droṇa's entry in the arena in the company of Aśvatthāman compared with the appearance of the Moon and Mars in the sky without clouds 1. 124. 18; Bāhlīka and Dhṛṣṭaketu, the king of the Cedis, fought each other as would Aṅgāraka and Budha 6. 43. 38; Drupada and Jayadratha fought each other as would Śukra and Aṅgāraka 6. 43. 54; Arjuna killed many Saṃśaptakas by adopting repeatedly oblique movements like Aṅgāraka (वक्रानुवक्रगमनाद् अङ्गारक इव ग्रहः) 8. 14. 1; Alambusa, in his duel with Ghaṭotkaca, fell down on the ground as would Aṅgāraka by chance (यदृच्छया निपतितम् अलम्बुसम् (7. 84. 26), भूमाव् अङ्गारकं यथा) 7. 84. 27; Bhūri, a Kaurava, when struck by the शक्ति of Sātyaki fell down on the ground from his chariot as would Mars, by chance, from the sky (लोहिताङ्ग इवाकाशाद् दीप्तरश्मिर् यद्-ऋच्छया) 7. 141. 12. 2. Omens: Vyāsa told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Aṇgāraka making re-trograde (वक्र) movement in the con-stellation Maghā indicated fierce destruction of the two armies (सेनयोर् अशिवं घोरं करिष्यति महाग्रहः । मघास्व् अङ्गारको वक्रः) 6. 3. 13; another bad omen pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra before the war was that Mars, the red-bodied one (लोहि-ताङ्ग), after making repeated retrograde movements and returning to the Brahmarāśi was established in the Śravaṇa नक्षत्र (वक्रानुवक्रं कृत्वा च श्रवणे पावक-प्रभः । ब्रह्मराशिं समावृत्य लोहिताङ्गो व्यवस्थितः । ) 6. 3. 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 18: तत्रैव सर्वतोभद्रचक्रे मघा-स्थो लोहिताङ्गो ऽङ्गारको वक्रानुवक्रं पुनःपुनर् वक्रीभूय ब्रह्मणा बृहस्-पतिनाक्रान्तम् राशिं नक्षत्रं श्रवणं समावृत्य सम्यक् पूर्णदृष्ट्या विद्ध्वा तिष्ठति); among the bad omens noticed by Karṇa and pointed out to Kṛṣṇa one referred to the retrograde motion of Mars in Jyeṣṭhā and his wooing Anurādhā thereby as though tran-quilizing the Maitra Nakṣatrayoga (कृत्वा चाङ्गारको वक्रं ज्येष्ठायां मधु-सूदन । अनुराधां प्रार्थयते मैत्रं संशमयन्न् इव ॥ ) 5. 141. 8 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 9: ज्येष्ठाम् अप्राप्य यदि भौमो वक्रीभवेत् तर्हि ज्येष्ठस्य राज्ञः ये ऽमित्रभूतास् ते सर्वे नश्येयुर् इति भावः । मैत्रं [मित्रसमूहं सं-गमयन् नाशयन् । “वैवस्वतं सं-गमनं जनानाम्” (RV. 10. 14. 1) इत्य् आदौ संपूर्वस्य गमेर् मारणार्थत्व-दर्शनात्).
अनुमति: Anumati f.: Name of the first Paurṇa-māsī day (when the Paurṇamāsī extends to two days; see Ait. Br. 32. 9 and Nirukta 11. 29). She, personified, arrived at the river Sarasvatī to be present at the investiture of Kumāra as the general of the gods 9. 44. 12, 16; she served as one of the reins (योक्त्राणि) of the horses of Śiva's chariot when it was made ready for his fight with the Tripuras 8. 24. 74.
अनुराधा: Anurādhā f.: Name of the seventeenth Nakṣatra. A. Religious rites: If one gives under the Nakṣatra Anurādhā, after observing fast, a gift of a covering (प्रावार) and another cloth (वस्त्रान्तर), he is glorified in the heaven for a hundred Yugas 13. 63. 22; if one offers a श्राद्ध under Anurādhā he establishes a line of kings (?राजचक्रम् प्रवर्तयेत्) 13. 89. 8. B. Bad omens: Among the bad omens reported by Karṇa to Kṛṣṇa there was one which referred to the retrograde motion of Mars (Aṅgāraka) in Jyeṣṭhā and his wooing Anurādhā thereby as though tranquilizing the Maitra Nakṣatra-yoga (कृत्वा चाङ्गारको वक्रं ज्येष्ठायां मधुसूदन । अनुराधां प्रार्थयते मैत्रं संशमयन्न् इव) 5. 141. 8 (For Nī. comm. see Aṅgāraka).
अभिजित्: Abhijit f.: Name of the twentieth Nakṣatra. Described as heavenly (देवी) 3. 219. 8; Indra reported to Skanda that Abhijit, the younger sister vying with Rohiṇī as she desired higher rank, went to the forest to practise austerities; Indra was, therefore, con-fused (in reckoning time) due to the dropping down of one Nakṣatra from the sky (अभिजित् स्पर्धमाना तु रोहिण्या कन्यसी स्वसा । इच्छन्ती ज्येष्ठतां देवी तपस् तप्तुं वनं गता ॥ तत्र मूढो ऽस्मि … नक्षत्रं गगनाच् च्युतम् । कालं त्व् इमं परं स्कन्द ब्रह्मणा सह चिन्तय) 3. 219. 8-9; (to fill the gap, the Kṛttikās went to the heaven 3. 219. 11) (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 230. 8-9, 11: कन्यसी कनिष्ठा वनं गता अधिकारं त्यक्त्वेति शेषः ॥ ८ । ।सा च ज्येष्ठतास्पर्-धया गगनात् च्युता अतो ऽहं मूढो ऽस्मि नक्षत्रसंख्यापूरणप्रकारस्याज्ञानाद् इति भावः ॥ ९ । ।तथा च कृत्तिकाभिर् एव नक्षत्रसंख्यापूर्तिं कुर्व् इति शक्राशयं ज्ञात्वा तास् त्रिदिवं गताः ॥ ११ । ।); if one offers a श्राद्ध under the constellation Abhijit he attains superior knowledge (विद्यां श्रेष्ठाम् अवाप्नुयात्) 13. 89. 11. [See Abhijita1]
अभिजित: Abhijita1 m.: Name of a Nakṣatra (= Abhijit ?) Here called योग; if a righteous person (धर्मनित्य) gives the gift of milk mixed with honey and घृत to learned men under the constellation Abhijita (अभिजिते योगे) he is honoured in heaven 13. 63. 27.

Abhijita2 m.: Name of the eighth part of the day (मुहूर्त), about mid-day (twenty-four minutes before and twenty-four minutes after midday). Yudhiṣṭhira was born at the Abhijita मुहूर्त (मुहूर्ते ऽभिजिते ऽष्टमे) 1. 114. 4 (Nī, however, on Bom. Ed. 1. 123. 6, takes अष्टमे to identify the नक्षत्र Jyeṣṭhā: ज्येष्ठानक्षत्रे अष्टमे संवत्सरारम्भात्)
अश्वयुज: Aśvayuja m.: Name of a constellation. Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a श्राद्ध (which is काम्य) under this constellation one got horses (अश्वांश् चाश्वयुजे वेत्ति) 13. 89. 14. [See Aśvinī]
अश्विनी: Aśvinī f.: Name of a constellation. Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that one who gave as gift a chariot with horses under the Aśvinī नक्षत्र, was born in a family that had many elephants, horses and chariots 13. 63. 34. [See Aśvayuja]
अषाढा: Aṣāḍhā f.: See Uttarāṣāḍhā and Pūrvāṣāḍhā.
अक्षयवट: Akṣayavaṭa m.: Name of a tree, also referred to as अक्षय्यकरणो वटः (3. 85. 8; 13. 88. 14). A. Location: Near Gayā (3. 82. 71-72; 13. 88. 14; 3. 85. 8); near the river Mahānadī and the lake Gayaśiras 3. 85. 8; 3. 93. 10 (where the lake Brahmasaras is also mentioned). B. Description: great (महन्त्) 3. 93. 13; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः) 3. 82. 72; famous in the worlds (प्रथितो लोकेषु) 13. 88. 14; praised by the Vipras (कीर्त्यते विप्रैः) 3. 85. 8. C. Explanation of the name: Since food offered to manes near this tree becomes inexhaustible (अक्षय), the tree is so called 13. 85. 8 (for citation see below section D.). D. Importance: Food offered to manes near this tree becomes inexhaustible (पितॄणां तत्र वै दत्तम् अक्षयं भवति प्रभो) 3. 82. 72; (यत्रा-सौ कीर्त्यते विप्रैर् अक्षय्यकरणो वटः । यत्र दत्तं पितृभ्यो ऽन्नम् अक्षयं भवति प्रभो ॥ ) 3. 85. 8; the Brāhmaṇas who came there in hundreds offered the Cātur-māsya sacrifices according to the ancient prescription (आर्षेण विधिना) and told pious tales of the high-souled in the सदस् (कथाः प्रचक्रिरे पुण्याः सदैसिथा महात्म-नाम्) 3. 93. 14-15. E. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas offered there the Cāturmāsya sacrifices and the great sacrifice to the ऋषिस् (तत्र ते पाण्डवा वीरा चातुर्मास्यैस् तदे-जिरे । ऋषियज्ञेन महता यत्राक्षयवटो महान्) 3. 93. 13.
अगस्त्यतीर्थ: Agastyatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (different from Agastyasaras). A. Location: One of the तीर्थस् on the southern ocean (समुद्रे तीर्थानि दक्षिणे) 1. 208. 3; on the ocean in the Draviḍa country (द्रविडेषु राजन् समुद्रम् आसाद्य … अगस्त्यतीर्थम् … ददर्श) 3. 118. 4; in the counry of the Pāṇḍyas (अगस्त्यतीर्थं पाण्ड्येषु) 3. 86. 10. B. Description: sanctifying and holy (पवित्रपुण्य) 3. 118. 4; holy for the worlds (लोकपुण्य) 3. 118. 4; very holy (सुपुण्य) 1. 208. 1; worshipped by the ascetics (सुपूजितानि तपस्विभिः) 1. 208. 1. C. History: It was once thronged by ascetics, but later avoided by them as the five crocodiles in the तीर्थ dragged some of them away; it then became isolated (विवि-क्तानि) 1. 208. 2, 4-6. D. Epic event: (1) Arjuna visited the five तीर्थस् and freed them of the crocodiles 1. 208. 7-21; 1. 209. 1-23; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira, with his brothers and wife, reached the तीर्थ and heard there the exploits of Arjuna and was highly grati-fied; he bathed there with his wife and bro-thers and extolled the heroism of Arjuna; he gave as gift a thousand cows and praised the gift of cows given by Arjuna (this gift of Arjuna is not reported earlier in the Adhyāyas 1. 208 and 209) (अर्जुनस्य संकीर्तयाम् आस गवां प्रदानम्) 3. 118. 4-7.
अगस्त्यवट: Agastyavaṭa m.: Name of a tree. A. Location: On the slope of the mountain Himavant (हिमवत्पार्श्वम्) and near the Vasiṣṭhaparvata and the Bhṛgutuṅga 1. 267. 1-2. B. Epic event: Arjuna, during his exile, reached there form the Gaṅgādvāra 1. 206. 6; 1. 207. 1-2.
अगस्त्यसरस्: Agastyasaras nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (different from Agastyātīrtha). A. Location: One can reach the Taṇ-ḍulikāśrama from the Jambūmārga, and from that आश्रम proceed to Agastyasaras 3. 80. 62-63. B. Importance: Pulastya told Bhīṣma that if one was engaged in the worship of manes and gods (पितृदेवार्चने रतः) at the Agastyasaras and observed fast for three nights he obtained the fruit of performing an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; and if one lived there on vegetables and fruits he obtained the place of Kumāra (कौमारं विन्दते पदम्) 3. 80. 63-64.
अग्नितीर्थ: Agnitīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Epic event: Balarāma in his तीर्थ-यात्रा, proceeded from Śamītīrtha to Agni-tīrtha; he bathed there and proceeded to the Brahmayoni तीर्थ 9. 46. 12, 20. B. My-thological event (which explains the name of the तीर्थ): God Fire, afraid of Bhṛgu's curse, entered a Śamī tree at this तीर्थ and disappeared (भृगोः शापाद् भृशं भीतो जातवेदाः प्रतापवान् । शमीगर्भम् अथासाद्य ननाश भगवांस् ततः ॥ ) 9. 46. 16; (नष्टो न दृश्यते यत्र शमीगर्भे हुताशनः) 9. 46. 12; the gods, in their search for Fire, reached Agnitīrtha and found Fire lying within the Śamī tree 9. 46. 12. C. Importance: Pulastya told Bhīṣma that by bathing at Agnitīrtha one reached the world of Agni and lifted up his family (अग्निलोकम् अवाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्-धरेत्) 3. 81. 119.
अग्निधारा: Agnidhārā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Famous in the three worlds 3. 82. 127; by visiting it one acquired the fruit of Agni-ṣṭoma sacrifice and did not return (to this world) from heaven (न च स्वर्गान् निवर्-तते) 3. 82. 127.
अग्निशिरस्: Agniśiras nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the river Yamunā 3. 88. 2, 6. B. Description: holy (पुण्य), heavenly (दिव्य), auspicīous (शिव) 3. 88. 4. C. Past events: (1) Sahadeva offered there sacrifices by measuring the sacrificial ground with the throw of a peg; with regard to this a गाथा, sung by Indra, was current in this world among the twice-born; it said that Sahadeva performed Agnicayana a hund-red hundred-thousand times along the river Yamunā and gave hundreds of thousands as दक्षिणा (सहदेवो ऽयजद् यत्र शम्याक्षे-पेण भारत ॥ एतस्मिन्न् एव चार्थेयम् इन्द्रगीता युधिष्ठिर । गाथा चरति लोके ऽस्मिन् गीयमाना दिविजातिभिः ॥ अग्नयः सहदेवेन ये चिता यमुनाम् अनु । शतम् शतसहस्राणि सहस्रशतदक्षिणाः ॥ ) 3. 88. 4-6 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 90. 5: शम्या-क्षेपेण बलवता क्षिप्ता शम्या लगुडविशेषो यावद् दूरं पतेत् तावान् यज्ञमण्डपो यस्मिन् यज्ञे स शम्याक्षेपः); (2) King Bharata, the famous emperor, offered there 35 horse sacrifices 3. 88. 7.
अग्नेः: Agneḥ puram nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Aṅgiras told Gautama that by bathing in this तीर्थ one becomes identical with ब्रह्मन् (अग्नेः पुरे नरः स्नात्वा … ब्रह्मभूतो विराजते) 13. 26. 41.
अङ्गारपर्ण: Aṅgāraparṇa nt.: Name of a forest. Located on the rivers Gaṅgā and Vākā; described as variegated (चित्र) 1. 158. 13; it belonged to the Gandharva Aṅgāra-parṇa, the beloved friend of Kubera, and he lived there; it was visited neither by corpses nor horned animals, nor gods, nor men (न कुणपाः शृङ्गिण्ō वा न देवा न च मानु-षाः । इदम् समुपसर्पन्ति) 1. 158. 13-14; the Pāṇḍavas encountered the Gandharva there while they were proceeding to the city of the Pāñcālas 1. 157. 15; 1. 158. 14.
अञ्जनाभ: Añjanābha m.: Name of a mountain. Finds place, with other mountains, in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 27; (13. 151. 2). [See Añjana]
अतिकृष्णा: Atikṛṣṇā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 23, 5; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 13; all the rivers are described as very strong and the mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35.
अद्रिजा: Adrijā f.: Name of a river (or an epithet of Kṛṣṇaveṇā ?) Finds place among the rivers listed in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa (गोदावरी च वेण्णा च कृष्णवेणा तथाद्रिजा) 13. 151. 17, 2.
अधिवंश्य: Adhivaṃśya nt.: Name of a sacred grove. By entering this sacred grove (तपोवन) one rejoiced among the Guhyakas; there was no doubt about this (गुह्यकेषु महाराज मोदते नात्र संशयः) 3. 82. 98.
अधृष्या: Adhṛṣyā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 23, 5; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 13; all rivers descri-fied as very strong and the mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35.
अनरक: Anaraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: A तीर्थ of all gods (तीर्थे तु सर्वदेवानाम्) 3. 81. 151, be-cause (1) there Brahmā himself is always waited upon (अन्वास्यते) by gods led by Nārāyaṇa 3. 81. 147; (2) Rudra's wife remains in vicinity; by paying a visit to the goddess one never meets with misfortunes (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 148; (3) There is also god Viśveśvara (Śiva), husband of Umā; by paying a visit to him one is freed of all sins (मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिशैः) 3. 81. 149; (4) By visiting there Padma-nābha Nārāyaṇa one shines and obtains the world of Viṣṇu (शोभमानो महाराज विष्णुलोकं प्रपद्यते) 3. 81. 150. B. Holiness: By bathing at Anaraka one does not meet with misfortunes (न दुर्-गतिम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 146, and, freed of all sorrow, he always shines like the moon (सर्वदुःखैः परित्यक्तो द्योतते शशिवत् सदा) 3. 81. 151.
अनाजन्मन्: Anājanman nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated to the east of the तीर्थ Saraka, it is famous (विश्रुत) and sacred to Nārada (नारदस्य महात्मनः । तीर्थम्); by bathing there and by giving up one's life, one goes, with the consent of Nārada, to the worlds that are difficult to obtain (नारदेना-भ्यनुज्ञातो लोकान् प्राप्नोति दुर्लभान्) 3. 81. 67-68.
अन्तःशिला: Antaḥśilā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 29, 5; its water is used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13; all these rivers are described as very strong (महाबलाः) and the mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) 6. 10. 35.
अन्तर्गिरि: Antargiri m.: Name (?) of a mountain. Situated in the north, it was conquered by Arjuna 2. 24. 2, 1.
अन्धकार: Andhakāra(ka) m.: Name of a moun-tain. Andhakāraka is situated in the Krauñca-dvīpa, beyond the mountain Vāmana(ka); beyond Andhakāra is the mountain Maināka 6. 13. 17-18.
अपरनन्दा: Aparanandā f.: Name of a river. A. Description: Destroying sin and danger (पापभयापहा) 3. 109. 1. B. Epic connections: (1) Arjuna, during his exile in the forest, saw it (1. 207. 7) while proceeding to the east (प्राचीं दिशम् अभिप्रेप्सुः) 1. 207. 5; after visiting these holy places Arjuna purified himself and gave wealth to Brāhmaṇas 1. 207. 8; (2) Yudhi-ṣṭhira reached it (3. 109. 1) from the Aga-styāśrama (3. 94. 1). C. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 23, 2.
अपरान्त: Aparānta m.: Name of a mountain. Brave Ketumant killed prince Sudar-śana at the mountain pass of the Aparānta (अपरान्तगिरिद्वारे) 7. 9. 40.

Aparānta m. (sg., pl.): Name of a Janapada. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (कुट्टापरान्ता द्वैधेस् याः) 6. 10. 47; it was along the coast of the southern ocean (गच्छ पारं समुद्रस्य दक्षिणस्य) 12. 49. 58; (also see the next section). B. Epic event: Kaśyapa told Rāma (Jāmadagnya): “Do not stay in my territory; go to the coast of the sou-thern ocean and live there” (न ते मद्-विषये राम वस्तव्यम् इह कर्हिचित्) 12. 49. 58; then the ocean, due to fear of Jāmadagnya, vacated some space called Śūrpāraka; that region came to be known as Aparānta (ततः शूर्पारकं देशं सागरस् तस्य निर्ममे । संत्रासाज् जाम-दग्न्यस्य सो ऽपरान्तं महीतलम् ॥ ) 12. 49. 59. C. Special feature: Known for sharp and long swords, lances, शक्तिस्, पर-श्वधस् and sharp axes which were pro-duced there (निशितांश् चैव दीर्घासीन् ऋष्टिशक्तिपरश्वधान् । अपरान्तसमुद्भू-तांस् तथैव परशूञ् शितान् ॥ ) 2. 47, 24. D. Epic event: The above arms were brought as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira by the people who came for his Rājasūya (बलिं च कृत्स्नम् आदाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 25.
अपां: Apāṃ hradaḥ m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma that one who practises chastity, has controlled his anger, is devoted to truth and does not cause injury to others (ब्रह्मचारी जितक्रोधः सत्य-संधस् त्व् अहिंसकः) bathes (उपस्पृश्य) at this तीर्थ, he obtains the merit of per-forming a Vājapeya sacrifice 13. 26. 13.
अमराणाम्: Amarāṇām hradaḥ m.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing at this तीर्थ one obtains the prowess of gods and is glorified among them in heaven (अमराणां ह्रदे स्नात्वा अमरेषु नराधिप । अमराणां प्रभा-वेन स्वर्गलोके महीयते) 3. 81. 89.
अम्बुवश्य: Ambuvaśya nt.: Name of a sacred place. The तीर्थस् sacred to Kośeśvara (Kubera ?) are located there (ततो ऽम्बुवश्यं धर्-मज्ञ समासाद्य यथाक्रमम् । कोशेश्व-रस्य तीर्थेषु); by bathing in these तीर्थस् one is freed of all diseases and is glorified in the Brahmaloka 3. 81. 46.
अम्बुवाहिनी: Ambuvāhinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 26, 5; its water used for drinking by people 6. 10. 13; all these rivers are described as very strong (महा-बलाः) and mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) 6. 10. 35; finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2.
अरण्या: Araṇyā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 33, 5; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13; all these rivers are described as very strong (महा-बलाः) and the mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) 6. 10. 35.
अरन्तुकस्य: Arantukasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। This तीर्थ sacred to Arantuka, lord of the Yakṣas, was situated on the river Sara-svatī (ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र द्वारपालम् अरन्तुकम् । तस्य तीर्थं सरस्वत्यां यक्षेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः); by bathing there one obtains the fruit of performing an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 81. 42.
अरुणा: Aruṇā f.: Name of a river; also called तीर्थ (9. 42. 26, 27). A. Description: An excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 42. 26; the confluence of the river Sarasvatī and Aruṇā was world famous (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 81. 131. B. Relation with other तीर्थस्: (1) The Devītīrtha (तीर्थं देव्याः) was situated near it 3. 81. 131; (2) The confluence of the rivers Kauśikī and Aruṇā was known as the Kālikā-saṃgama 3. 82. 135. C. Importance: (1) A bath in the river Aruṇā frees one of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (ब्रह्म-हत्यापहा हि सा) 9. 42. 25, 34; (2) If one fasts for three nights and bathes at the confluence of Aruṇā and Sarasvatī one is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa and he obtains the fruit of performing an Agni-ṣṭoma and an Atirātra sacrifice; he also purifies his lineage for seven generations 3. 81. 131-32; he is also freed of all sins 3. 82. 135; (3) Aruṇā finds mention in the Dai-vata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16. D. Events: (1) Epic: (a) Before starting the war on the eighteenth day, the Kaurava warriors went to the rivers Aruṇā and Sarasvatī and bathed there and drank their water; the place was situated on the slope of Himavant a little less than two योजनस् from the Kuru-kṣetra (ऊने द्वियोजने गत्वा प्रत्यतिष्ठन्त कौरवाः । … प्रस्थे हिमवतः शुभे) 9. 4. 48-49; the warriors returned from there for war with their energies restored (कृतोत्-साहाः) 9. 4. 50; (b) Balarāma bathed in Aruṇā, gave varied gifts and acquired religi-ous merit (अवाप्य धरमम्) 9. 42. 38; (2) Mythological; (a) when the ascetics requested Sarasvatī for the मोक्ष of the Rākṣasas, it brought to its body the river Aruṇā (अरुणाम् आनयाम् आस स्वां तनुं पुरुषर्षभ) 9. 42. 24; when the Rākṣasas bathed in Aruṇā they left their bodies and went to heaven (तनूस् त्यक्त्वा दिवं गताः) 9. 42. 25; (b) Indra was advised by Brahmadeva to perform a sacrifice on the river Sarasvatī and to bathe in Aruṇā according to the prescribed rites (यथाविधि 9. 42. 34); he was then freed of the sin arising out of killing a Brāhmaṇa (अरुणा-याम् उपास्पृशत् । स मुक्तः पाप्मना तेन ब्रह्मह्यत्याकृतेन ह) 9. 42. 35-36; 9. 42. 26; (c) Namuci's head too reached the eternal, wish-yielding worlds by plung-ing (आप्लुत्य) into Aruṇā (शिरश् तच् चापि नमुचेः लोकान् कामदुघान् प्राप्तम् अक्षयान्) 9. 42. 37.
अरुन्धतीवाट: Arundhatīvāṭa m.: Name of a तीर्थ (?) One who is on a pilgrimage (तीर्थ-सेवी) is advised by Pulastya to visit Arun-dhatīvaṭa 3. 82. 37 (Name of a banyan tree situated near the Sāmudraka तीर्थ ?).
अलकनन्दा: Alakanandā f.: Name of a river. Arjuna told the Gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa that when the holy river Gaṅgā flows through the sky the river has only one bank; there, among the gods, it obtains the status of Alakanandā (इयं भूत्वा चैकवप्रा शुचिर् आकाशगा पुनः । देवेषु गङ्गा गन्धर्व प्राप्नोत्य् अलकनन्दताम्) 1. 158. 18 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 170 21: एकम् आकाशरूपं वप्रं तटं यस्याः सा).
अलम्ब: Alamba nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Garuḍa, on his way to fetch अमृत (सोम) from heaven, goes to Alambatīrtha holding an elephant and a tortoise, one each in his two claws; in the vicinity of this तीर्थ there are divine trees (देववृक्षान् उपागमत्) 1. 25. 27.
अवतीर्ण: Avatīrṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Situated near the con-fluence of the river Sarasvatī and the river Aruṇā 3. 81. 133, (131). B. Origin: It was created in the bygone days by Darbhin for he was compassionate to the Brāhmaṇas (विप्राणाम् अनुकम्पार्थं दर्भिणा निर्-मितं पुरा) 3. 81. 133; while creating it Darbhin had brought together waters of the four oceans (समुद्राश् चापि चत्वारः समानीताश् च दर्भिणा) 3. 81. 136. C. Importance: Even if one has not performed the sacred rites nor recited the मन्त्रस्, if he bathes in this तीर्थ he is as good as one who has observed the vows-this is declared in an ancient text (?) (दृष्टम् एतत् पुरा-तने) 3. 81. 135; one who bathes in the तीर्थ does not meet with adversity (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नुयात्) und he obtains the fruit of donating four thousand cows 3. 81. 136.
अशोकतीर्थ: Aśokatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the south (3. 86. 1) in the land of the Martyas (? मर्त्येषु; v. 1. मत्-स्येषु) 3. 86. 10; there were many आश्रमस् around it (बहुलाश्रम) 3. 86. 10.
अश्वतीर्थ: Aśvatīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: The bank of the Ganges, not far from the city Kanyakubja, “is even now known as Aśvatīrtha” (अदूरे कन्य-कुब्जस्य गङ्गायास् तीरम् उत्तमम् । अश्व-तीर्थं तद् अद्यापि मानवाः परिचक्षते) 13. 4. 17; one of the तीर्थस् on Gomatī 3. 93. 2. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 93. 2. C. Origin: Varuṇa gave to Bhārgava Ṛcīka one thousand white (पाण्-डुर), shining like the moon (चन्द्र-वर्चस्), and swift (तरस्विन्) horses who had a black ear on one side (एकतःश्याम-कर्ण); the horses were meant to be given by Ṛcika to Gādhi, king of Kanyakubja, as a dowry for marrying his daughter 3. 115. 9, 12; 5. 117. 5; 13. 4. 14, 16; the place where the horses emerged from the water of Gaṅgā (13. 4. 16) came to be known as Aśvatīrtha (तद् अश्वतीर्थं वि-ख्यातम् उत्थिता यत्र ते हयाः) 3. 115. 16; 5. 117. 6. D. Religious importance: After bathing there, the Pāṇḍavas gave away cows and riches 3. 93. 2; they repeatedly offered there offerings to gods and manes and satisfied the Brāhmaṇas (तत्र देवान् पितॄन् विप्रांस् तर्पयित्वा पुनः पुनः) 3. 93. 3.
अश्वनदी: Aśvanadī f.: Name of a river. Kuntī placed the newly born Karṇa in a basket covered with wax (मञ्जूषायाम् … मधूच्छिष्टस्थितायाम्) and released it in the river Aśvanadī 3. 292. 7, 9, 22, 25 (from where it went to the river Carmaṇvatī, Yamunā and finally to Gaṅgā).
अश्वरथा: Aśvarathā f.: Name of a river. Draupadī pointed out to Bhīma on the mountain Gandhamādana (Himavant) that flowers of five colours which were blown there by wind, produced by speed of Suparṇa, were dropped in the river Aśvarathā-a sight watched by all creatures (प्रत्यक्षं सर्व-भूतानाम्) 3. 157. 19.
अस्वशिरस्: Asvaśiras nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 7. 57. 28. B. Epic events connected with this तीर्थ: (1) The sage Bṛhadaśva taught अक्षहृदय (the secret science of the game of dice), which he knew thoroughly well (3. 78. 15), to Yudhiṣṭhira (to dispel the latter's fear of losing everything once again in the game of dice), and then went to Aśvaśiras to bathe (दत्त्वा चाश्वशिरो ऽगच्-छद् उपस्प्रष्टुं महातपाः) 3. 78. 17 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 79. 21: अश्वशिरो ऽस्वविद्याम् यया बृहदश्व इति मुनेर् नाम । उपस्प्रष्टुं स्नानादिकं कर्तुम्) (this Aśvaśiras apparently was in the vicinity of the Kāmyaka forest where Bṛhadaśva met the Pāṇḍavas 3. 49. 2, 29); (2) Arjuna, on his way to the mountain Himavant to receive the Pāśupata अस्त्र from Śiva crossed many places near the Himavant, one of them being Aśvaśiras 7. 57. 28 (this Aśvaśiras seems to be different from the one referred to in the above event).
अश्विनोस्: Aśvinos tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ sacred to the Aśvins. By visiting this तीर्थ of the Aśvins one becomes handsome (अश्विनोस् तीर्थम् आसाद्य रूपवान् अभिजायते) 3. 81. 14.
अष्टावक्र: Aṣṭāvakra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who offers libation of water to manes at Aṣṭāvakra and fasts for twelve days obtains the fruit of performing a human sacrifice (नरमेधफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 39 (situated near Haridwar, see Editor's note on the stanza, Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, part II, p. 1067).
असिक्नी: Asiknī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 22, 5; its water is used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13.
असिपत्रवन: Asipatravana nt.: Name of a forest (?) Yudhiṣṭhira while going in the company of the Devadūta to see his brothers after their death passed through Asipatravana (lit. ‘a forest having leaves as sharp as the blade of a sword’) which was covered with sharp razors (निषितक्षुरसंवृत) 18. 2. 23; a wicked king, after death, before going to hell is merged in the hot Vaitaraṇī river and then gets his body pricked in the Asi-patravana (असिपत्रवनभिन्नगात्रः) 12. 309. 31.
अस्त: Asta m.: Name of a mountain, also called once Astaṃgiri (7. 31. 77). A. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 15. 39. 24; the best among the mountains (गिरि-श्रेष्ठ) 6. 51. 40; (पर्वतश्रेष्ठ) 10. 1. 24; (गिरिवर) 15. 39. 24; sages call it the king of the mountains (अस्तं पर्व-तराजानम् एतम् आहुर् मनीषिणः) 3. 160. 10, 11. B. Relationship (1) with sun: The sun approaches it at sunset 1. 43. 23; 1. 143. 17; 3. 280. 17; 5. 108. 6; 5. 180. 39; 5. 182. 16; 5. 183. 26; 6. 51. 40, 43; 6. 82. 41; 6. 90. 46 (सूर्यास्तमनवेला for सूर्-यास्तमयनवेला ?); 7. 31. 77; 7. 48. 41; 7. 56. 22; 7. 121. 45; 7. 128. 10; 8. 21. 35; 9. 28. 62, 82; 10. 1. 24; 12. 58. 28; 12. 306. 12; 12. 318. 7; 15. 39. 24; the sun always sets only at the proper time (भानुः … नाकालतो ऽस्तं गिरिम् अभ्युपैति) 12. 26. 12; the sun having reached the Asta mountain and going beyond the dusk repairs to the north; then going round the mountain Meru he moves towards the east (अस्तं प्राप्य ततः सं-ध्याम् अतिक्रम्य दिवाकरः । उदीचीं भ-जते काष्ठां दिशम् एष विभावसुः ॥ स मेरुम् अनुवृत्तः सन् पुनर् गच्छति पाण्डव । प्राङ्मुखः सविता देवः) 3. 160. 25-26; the answer to the question: “who leads the sun to the Asta ?”, the reply is: “Dharma leads the sun to the Asta and there it rests in truth” (कश् चैनम् अस्तं नयति … धर्मश् चास्तं नयति सत्ये च प्रतितिष्ठति) 3. 297. 26-27; (सत्येन प्रति-तिष्ठति) 3. 160. 10; (2) with dusk: the latter twilight (dusk) proceeds from it (अस्तो नाम यतः संध्या पश्चिमा प्रतिसर्पति) 5. 108. 6; (3) with nights: they go to the Asta mountain (अस्तं गच्छन्ति रात्रयः) 12. 318. 8; (4) with the luminaries: they return to the Asta mountain at the end of the night 7. 171. 4; (5) with clouds: Asta, together with Udaya, receives a large number of big clouds (प्रत्यगृह्णात् … महामेघान् इव बहुञ् शैलाव् अस्तोदयाव् उभौ) 9. 15. 31. C. Importance: King Varuṇa lives on the Asta mountain and in the great ocean and from there protects the beings (अस्तं पर्वतराजानं समुद्रं च महोदधिं । आवसन् वरुणो राजा भूतानि परिरक्षति) 3. 160. 11. D. Similes: (1) Falling down of the head of Daṇḍa, red-coloured, when cut off by Arjuna, compared with the falling down of the sun to the west from the Asta mountain 8. 13. 19; (2) Falling down of the excellent, bright diadem of Arjuna, compared with the burning sun falling down from the Asta mountain 8. 66. 16; (3) Karṇa, circled by the network of the arrows shot from his bow, appeared like the sun, having the circle of red rays, pro-ceeding toward the Asta mountain 8. 66. 40; (4) Duryodhana and Śalya received the warriors rushing at them as do the Asta and the Udaya mountains the clouds 9. 15. 31; (5) the arrows shot at Bhīma by Aśvatthā-man proceeded towards him like the luminaries proceeding towards the Asta mountain at the end of the night 7. 171. 4; (6) Bhīṣma's downfall, after he had tormented the enemies with the heat of his weapons, compared with the setting of the sun (नरसूर्यो ऽस्तम् अभ्येति सूर्यो ऽस्तम् इव केशव) 11. 23. 16; (7) (i) Vicitravīrya's going to the abode of Yama (his death) compared with the sun's going to the Asta (जगामास्तम् इवादित्यः कौरव्यो यमसादनम्) 1. 96. 58; (ii) Vyuṣitāśva's death compared with the sun's going to the Asta (जगामास्तम् इवांशुमान्) 1. 112. 17. E. Use of the expression अस्तम् इ or गम् to mean ‘die’: अस्तम् इते भीष्मे 12. 46. 23; (व्युषिताश्वः) जगामा-स्तम् 1. 112. 17.
अहुर्: Ahur nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Difficult to reach (सुदुर्लभ) 3. 81. 84; by bathing there one goes to the world of the sun (सूर्यलोकम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 84.
अहल्यायाः: Ahalyāyāḥ hradaḥ m.: Name of a sacred lake. Situated in the forest of Gautama 3. 82. 93; having bathed in the lake of Ahalyā (अहल्यायाः ह्रदे स्नात्वा) one attains (after death) the highest condition; acquiring lustre, he attains the highest glory (व्रजेत् परमां गतिम् । अभिगम्य श्रियं राजन् विन्दते श्रियम् उत्तमाम्) 3. 82. 93; there is also a well (उदपान) there which is famous in the three worlds; by taking bath in that well one obtains the fruit of perform-ing a horse sacrifice (तत्राभिषेकं कृत्वा तु वाजिमेधम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 82. 94.
अगस्त्यशिष्यस्य: Agastyaśiṣyasya āśramaḥ m.: See Tṛṇasomāgner āśramaḥ.
अगस्त्यस्य: Agastyasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। An आश्रम established by Agastya in the south (दक्षिणस्यां … शृणु तीर्थानि  … कीर्त्यमानानि) 3. 86. 1; located near the Vaiḍūrya mountain (वैडूर्यपर्वतस् तत्र  … अगस्त्यस्याश्रमश् चैव) 3. 86. 15; des-cribed as having many roots and fruits and ample water (बहुमूलफलोदक) 3. 86. 15.
अगस्त्याश्रम: Agastyāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम of Agastya, also called Hiraṇyabindu (3. 85. 15). A. Location: In the east (प्राचीम् दि-शं … कीर्तयिष्यामि) 3. 85. 3; in the vicinity of the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā at Prayāga (प्रयागम् इति विख्यातम् … अगस्त्यस्य … तत्राश्रमवरः) 3. 85. 13-15; on the Kālañjara mountain, known there as Hiraṇyabindu (हिरण्यबिन्दुः कथितो गिरौ कालञ्जरे नृप) 3. 8. 15; near the place called Durjayā (अगस्त्याश्र-मम् आसाद्य दुर्जयायाम् उवास ह) 3. 94. 1. B. Description: Excellent (आश्रमवर) 3. 85. 15; extensive (महन्त्) 3. 85. 15; well known (ख्यात) 3. 97. 26; pleasing (रम-णीय) 3. 97. 27; having (all) qualities (गुनैर् युतः) 3. 97. 27; having flowers of all seasons (सर्वर्तुकुसुमान्वित) 3. 97. 26. C. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas, in their तीर्थयात्रा, reached this आश्रम and lived there for some time 3. 94. 1. D. Past events: (1) Vātāpi was made quiet there (put out of action) by Agastya (अगस्त्ये-नेह वातापिः … उपशामितः) 3. 94. 2; (वातापिर् अगस्त्येन विनाशितः) 3. 97. 26; (2) Wealth given by Ilvala to Agastya, after the destruction of Vātāpi, was loaded on a chariot and carried to Agastyāśrama 3. 97. 15; (3) Gods, as directed by Viṣṇu, went to Agastyāśrama (to request him to drink up the ocean) and saw him in his आश्रम 3. 101. 11-13.
अच्युतस्थल: Acyutasthala nt.: Name of a town. A place in the Āraṭṭa (Bāhlīka) coun-try; one who stays there (long) cannot go to heaven; hence one should not stay there for more than a day—this is what a Brāh-maṇa told in the assembly of the Kurus (यद् अन्यो ऽप्य् उक्तवान् सभ्यो ब्राह्मणः कुरुसं सदि ॥ … प्रोष्य चाप्य् अच्युतस्थले ।  … कथं स्वर्गं गमिष्यति ॥ … आरट्टा नाम बाह्लीका न तेष्व् आर्यो द्व्यहं वसेत्  ॥ ) 8. 30. 41-43; the place also mentioned in what a Piśācī said to a Brāhmaṇī (?) who came to stay at Raupyā with her sons; this was told by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira when he wanted to recite the अनुवंश stanzas about Raupyā; according to the Piśācī no one who had stayed at Acyuta-sthala was supposed to stay near Raupyā for more than one night (अत्रानुवंशं पठतः शृणु मे कुरुनन्दन । … पिशाची यद् अभाषत । … उषित्वा चाच्युतस्थले॑ … एकरात्रम् उषित्वेह द्वितीयां यदि वत्स्यसि । एतद् वै ते दिवा वृत्तं रात्रौ वृत्तम् अतो ऽन्यथा ॥ ) 3. 129. 8-10; (according to the प्राञ्चः, whose view is cited by Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 9, one could stay at Raupyā even after staying at Acyutasthala if he had performed the prescribed प्रायश्चित्त viz. the प्राजापत्य व्रत; according to these प्राञ्चः, Acyutasthala was the village where people born of mixed marriages lived (अच्युतस्थलाख्ये संकरजानां ग्रामे); according to others, however, who under-stood the word in good light, Acyutasthala meant the subtle body (लिङ्गशरीर) and उषित्वा meant by being near the सूत्रात्मन् (सूत्रात्मानम् उपास्य)).
अन्ताखी: Antākhī (?) f.: Name of a city. A city outside the Bhāratavarṣa; Saha-deva brought it under control just by send-ing messengers and made its people pay tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (अन्ताखीं चैव रोमां च … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28 49. [See F. Edgerton JAOS 58. 264-265, 1938]
अपरपर्यट: Aparaparyaṭa nt.: Name of a city. In the west; one of the cities brought under control (वशे चक्रे) by Nakula in his expedition before the Rājasūya 2. 29. 10.
अभिसारी: Abhisārī f.: Name of a city. Situated in the north-west near the Trigartas; described as attractive (रम्या); Arjuna conquered it in his expedition to the north-west and north before the Rāja-sūya 2. 24. 18, 17.
अमरावती: Amarāvatī, Amarāvati (म्। च्। 3. 170. 25) f.: Name of Indra's city. A. City of Indra (शक्रस्य पुरीम्  … अमरावतीम्) 3. 43. 38; (शक्रस्य दयि-तां पुरीम्) 3. 44. 7; 1. 168. 20; 13. 31. 18; (देवराजस्य … अमरावती) 5. 101. 1; (शक्रस्य भवनम् … अमरावतीम्) 3. 164. 42; (महेन्द्रभवन) 7. 10. 22; (पुरन्-दरपुर) 3. 169. 27. B. Description: Pleasing (रम्या) 3. 44. 1; (पुरीं रम्-याम्) 3. 164. 51; excellent city (पुरी वर्या) 5. 101. 1; adorned with jewels (रत्नैश् च समलंकृताम्) 3. 164. 42; beautified with holy trees blossoming in all seasons (सर्व-र्तुकुसुमैः पुण्यैः पादपैर् उपशोभि-ताम्) 3. 44. 1; adorned with celestial trees giving the desired fruits (दिव्यैः काम-फलवृक्षैः … समलंकृताम्) 3. 164. 42; cold and holy winds carrying the fragrance of flowers blew there (पाण्डवः । पुष्प-गन्धवहैः पुण्यैर् वायुभिश् चानुवीजितः) 3. 44. 9; (शीतस् तत्र ववौ वायुः सुगन्धो जीवनः शुचिः) 3. 164. 47; resorted to by Siddhas and Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेविता) 3. 44. 1; Gandharvas and Apsarases pre-sent there 3. 44. 9; for the description of Śakra's residence (शक्रस्य भवनम् अम-रावतीम्, सुरवेश्मन्) see also 3. 164. 43-48. C. Characteristics: (1) विमानस् of gods, moving at will, in very large numbers, standing and going around (तत्र देव-विमानानि कामगानि सहस्रशः । संस्थितान्य् अभियातानि ददर्शायुतशस् तदा) 3. 44. 8; (2) Not easy to obtain: Maheśvara told Umā that a Dīkṣita who, while living in the company of deer, lives only on grass that falls down from the mouth of deer, will go to Amarāvatī (शष्पं मृगमु-खोत्सृष्टं यो मृगैः सह सेवते । दीक्षितो वै मुदा युक्तः स गच्छत्य् अमरा-वतीम् ॥ ) 13. 130. 40; also see section G below. D. Epic events: (1) Arjuna saw Amarāvatī in the Devaloka 3. 43. 14; 3. 164. 42. (2) Arjuna, when he saw the town of the Nivātakavacas, found it to be superior to the city of the gods and also to the city of Indra (विशिष्टं देवनगरात्) 3. 169. 26; (पुरन्दरपुराद् धीदं विशिष्टम् इति लक्षये) 3. 169. 27; he asked Mātali why the gods did not live in that city 3. 169. 26-27. E. Past event: Kṛṣṇa, mounted on Vainateya (Garuḍa), frightened (the denizens of) Amarāvatī (त्रासयित्वामरावतीम्) and brought Pārijāta from Indra's residence (महेन्द्रभवनात्) 7. 10. 22. F. Similes: (1) When king Saudāsa returned to the city of Ayodhyā it shone like Amarāvatī with Indra (शक्रेणे-वामरावती) 1. 168. 20; (2) Divodāsa built Vārāṇasī like Amarāvatī of Śakra 13. 31. 18; (3) Hiraṇyapura of the Kālakeya demons, which could move at will, was like Amarāvatī (अमरावतिसंकाशं पुरं कामगमं तु तत्) 3. 170. 25; (4) The town Bhogavatī of Vāsuki was like Amarā-vatī of Indra (यादृशी देवराजस्य पुरी यर्यामरावती) 5. 101. 1. G. Mode of expression: (1) To express great wonder: King Kuśika, seeing many wonderful things in the forest, wondered whether he had reached Uttara Kurus or Amarāvatī 13. 54. 16; (2) To express unattainability: Kṛṣṇa told Subhadrā that Jayadratha, even if he entered Amarāvatī, would not get away from Arjuna 7. 54. 19.
अयोध्या: Ayodhyā f.: Name of a city, also called Kosalā (3. 75. 3; 3. 263. 29). A. Location: In the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति) 2. 26. 1. B. Des-cription: Pleasing (रम्या) 3. 63. 19; 3. 275. 36; excellent, best town (पुरवर) 1. 168. 14; (पुरम् उत्तमम्) 1. 168. 19; famous (ख्यात) 1. 168. 14; city of the righteous (नगरीं पुण्यकर्मणाम्) 1. 168. 16; full of people who were contend-ed and well fed (तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा) 1. 168. 20. C. Epic event: Bhīma defeated king Dīrghaprajña of Ayodhyā in his ex-pedition to the east before the Rājasūya 2. 27. 2. D. Past events: (1) Events related to Rāmāyaṇa: (i) When Lakṣmaṇa was held and dragged towards his mouth by Kabandha, he lost hope of meeting Rāma again when he, with Sītā, would return to Kosalā (नाहं त्वाम् … कोसलागतं । द्रक्ष्यामि) 3. 263. 29; (ii) Rāma won-dered whether he would rule over Ayodhyā again after killing the enemies in battle and after getting Sītā back 3. 266. 34; (iii) After the सत्यक्रिया of Sītā, Rāma told Daśaratha that he would return to Ayodhyā at his bidding; Daśaratha asked him to go to Ayodhyā and rule over it 3. 275. 36-37; (iv) On reaching Ayodhyā, Rāma sent Ha-nūmant to Bharata 3. 275. 59; (2) Events related to the story of Nala: (i) Vārṣṇeya, the charioteer of Nala, left Nala's children with king Bhīma of Kuṇḍinapura and went to Ayodhyā to seek service with king Ṛtuparṇa 3. 57. 22; (ii) Karkoṭaka nāga advised Nala to assume the name Bāhuka and go to king Ṛtuparṇa of Ayodhā 3. 63. 19; Nala, accordingly, reached the town of Ṛtuparṇa (ऋतुपर्णस्य नगरम्) 3. 64. 1; (iii) The Brāhmaṇa Parṇāda told Dama-yantī that he had reached Ayodhyā in search of Nala; Damayantī wanted Sudeva to be sent back to Ayodhyā to get Nala; Damayantī sent Sudeva to Ṛtuparṇa resid-ing at Ayodhyā (hence called Ayodhyāpati in 3. 69. 22) to announce to him that she de-sired another husband and for this she was arranging another Svayaṃvara (ऋतुपर्णं वचो ब्रूहि पतिम् अन्यंचिकीर्षति । आस्थास्यति पुनर् भैमी दमयन्ती स्वयंवरम् ॥ ) 3. 68. 2, 16, 21; 3. 72. 17; (iv) Damayantī later told Nala that the Brāhmaṇa Parṇāda, while searching Nala, had reached the resi-dence of king Ṛtuparṇa in Kosalā (अभ्य-गच्छत् कोसलायाम् ऋतुपर्णनिवेशने) 3. 75. 3; (3) Other events: (i) Śaśāda ruled over Ayodhyā after Ikṣvāku 3. 193. 1; (ii) Parīkṣit, of Ikṣvāku family, once ruled over Ayodhyā 3. 190. 3; (iii) Gālava took Mādhavī with him and went to king Haryaśva of Ikṣvāku family who ruled at Ayodhyā 5. 113. 18; (iv) King Kalmāṣa-pāda, when freed from Rakṣas by Vasiṣṭha, returned to Ayodhyā; his subjects greeted him; Kalmāṣapāda entered the city with Vasiṣṭha; the citizens of Ayodhyā saw their king with Vasiṣṭha as the sun rising in conjunction with Puṣya; the city, with its streets cleansed and sprinkled with water and decorated with raised flags, pleased Kalmāṣapāda; when the king entered the city Ayodhyā with Vasiṣṭha, the queen, at the king's command, approached Vasiṣṭha for a son 1. 168. 14-19, 21. E. Similes: (1) Ayodhyā made prosperous by Kalmāṣa-pāda compared with the sky made to shine at the rise of the autumnal moon (स हि तां पूरयाम् आस लक्ष्म्या … । अयोध्यां व्योम शीतांशुः शरत्काल इवोदितः ॥ ) 1. 168. 18; (2) Ayodhyā, with its citizens contended and well nourished shone in the reign of Kalmāṣapāda as Amarāvatī due to Śakra (अशोभत तदा तेन शक्रेणेवामरावती) 1. 168. 20.
अलका: Alakā1 f.: Name of a lotus pond near the Sabhā of Kubera. Wind, carrying the fragrance from the lotus pond Alakā and giving delight to mind and heart, waits on Kubera in his Sabhā (आदाय गन्धान् … नलिन्याश् चालका-ख्यायाः … मनोहृदयसंह्लादी वायुस् तम् उपसेवते) 2. 10. 7-8.
Alakā2 f.: Name of the city of Kubera. Kubera is called the ‘lord of Alakā’ (अलकाधिप) 9. 10. 48; 12. 75. 4, 15.
अवन्ती: Avantī f.: Name of a city. Nala showed Damayantī the paths which, after crossing Avantī and Ṛkṣavant mountain, led to the Dakṣiṇāpatha (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्थानो दक्षिणापथम् । अवन्तीम् ऋक्षवन्तं च समतिक्रम्य पर्-वतम् ॥ ) 3. 58. 20. [Avanti, name of a Janapada, Section I. 6]
अश्वमेध: Aśvamedha m.: Name of a town (?). In the east (प्राचीम् दिशम्) 2. 26. 1, 7; Bhīma, in his expedition before the Rājasūya, conquered Rocamāna, king of Aśvamedha (सो ऽश्वमेधेश्वरं राजन् रोचमानम् … । जिगाय समरे वीरः … ॥ ) 2. 26. 8.
अहिच्छत्रा: Ahicchatrā f.: Name of a city. Situated in the territory called Ahic-chatra; described as having many commu-nities (जनपदायुता); it was conquered by Arjuna for Droṇa (अहिच्छत्रं च विषयं द्रोणः समभिपद्यत । एवं राजन्न् अहि-च्छत्रा पुरी जनपदायुता । युधि निर्जित्य पार्थेन द्रोणाय प्रतिपादिता ॥ ) 1. 128. 18.
अ: A Location: In the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशम्) 2. 24. 1. B. Des-cription: Delightful (रम्य) 2. 24. 19. C. Epic event: It was ruled by Cirāyudha: Arjuna defeated him in battle in his expedi-tion to the north of Indraprastha before the Rājasūya (ततः सिंहपुरं रम्यं चित्रायुधसुरक्षितम् । प्रामथद् … पाक-शासनिर् आहवे ॥ ) 2. 24. 19.
अकृष्ट: Akṛṣṭa m. (pl.): A class of sages. Mentioned among those sages who observed the eternal Vedic धर्म pre-scribed by Brahman after creating the world (सर्वलोकपितामहः । शाश्वतं वेदपठितं धर्मं च युयुजे पुनः ॥ ॥।अकृष्टाश् चैव हंसाश् च ऋषयो … स्थिता ब्रह्मानुशासने ॥ ) 12. 160. 21. 25.
अग्नियोनिज: Agniyonija m. (pl.): A class of sages. Mentioned among those who after the creation of the world followed the instruc-tion of Brahman and observed the eternal Vedic धर्म (ऋषयो ऽथाग्नियोनिजाः । … स्थिता ब्रह्मानुशासने ॥ ) 12. 160. 21, 25.
अग्निवेश्य: Agniveśya m. (pl.): Name of a people. The Agniveśya warriors were stationed on the left side of the Krauñcāruṇa Vyūha of the army of the Pāṇḍavas on the second day of the battle (अग्निवेश्या जगत्तुण्डाः  … वामं पार्श्वं समाश्रिताः) 6. 46. 51 (39, 50).
अङ्ग: Aṅga, Aṅgaka m. (pl., also sg.), Aṅgaviṣaya m. (sg.): Name of a country and its people; often mentioned along with Vaṅga and Kaliṅga. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the Janapadas of the Bhārata-varṣa (अङ्गा वङ्गाः कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 44, 5, 37; mentioned among the eastern countries, holy places in which were visited by Arjuna (प्राचीम् दिशम् अभि-प्रेप्सुर् जगाम) 1. 207. 5; (अङ्गवङ्ग-कलिङ्गेषु यानि पुण्यानि कानिचित् । जगाम तानि सर्वाणि) 1. 207. 9; the army prote-cted by the king of the Aṅga country (Karṇa) said to be of the easterners (तद् अङ्गपतिना गुप्तं … प्राच्यानाम् अभवद् बलम्) 6. 17. 28. B. Capital town: The capital of the Aṅga country was Campā (जगाम चम्पां प्रदिधक्षमाणस् तम् अङ्गराजं विषयं च तस्य) 3. 113. 15; also called Mālinī (मालिनीं नगरीम् … । अङ्गेषु) 12. 5. 6. C. Characteristics of the people: The people of the Aṅga and Kalinga country were mentioned by Karṇa among those peoples who knew eternal धर्म (कोसलाः काशयोऽङ्गाश् च कलिङ्गा  … । धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61; according to Karṇa the old men of the Aṅgaka, Kaliṅgaka and some other cou-ntries lived according to the धर्म taught to them (कालिङ्गकाश् चाङ्गका … शिष्टान् धर्मान् उपजीवन्ति वृद्धाः) 8. 30. 75; (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 8. 45. 30; स्व-यं धर्मस्वरूपम् अजानन्तो ऽपि शिष्टानु-गामिन इत्य् अर्थः); according to Śalya, however, people of the Aṅga country for-sook the sick people and sold their wives and children (आतुराणाम् परित्यागः स्व-दारसुतविक्रयः । अङ्गेषु वर्तते कर्ण) 8. 30. 83; D. Aṅga warriors: Specially skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गजयोधिनः, गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 1-3; (शिक्षिता हस्तिसादिनः) 7. 68. 31; also cf. 8. 12. 59; (आचार्यपुत्रे … हस्तिशिक्षावि-शारदे 8. 17. 15-18; 8. 49. 79. E. Epic events: (1) Child Karṇa, who was picked up by Adhiratha and Rādhā, grew up in the Aṅga country (स ज्येष्ठपुत्रः सूतस्य ववृधेऽङ्गेषु) 3. 293. 14; (2) Duryo-dhana said that if Arjuna was unwilling to fight with one who was not a king, he would make Karṇa the king of the Aṅga country; immediately afterwards the cere-mony of consecration of Karṇa as the ruler of the Aṅga country was duly per-formed by those who knew the मन्त्रस् (यद्य् अयं फल्गुनो युद्धे नाराज्ञा योद्धुम् इच्छति । तस्माद् एषो ऽङ्गविषये मया राज्ये ऽभिषिच्यते ॥ … ततस् तस्मिन् क्षणे कर्णः … अभिषिक्तो ऽङ्गराज्ये सः … ॥ ) 1. 126. 35-36; Karṇa whose head was moist due to water of consecration as a king of the Aṅga country was embraced by Adhiratha (परिष्वज्य च तस्याथ मूर्धानम् … अङ्गराज्याभिषेकार्द्रम्) 1. 127. 4; when Bhīma said that Karṇa did not deserve to be a king of the Aṅgas, Duryodhana retorted that Karṇa deserved not only to be the king of the Aṅgas but of the whole earth (अङ्गराज्यं च नार्हस् त्वम् उपभोक्तुम्) 1. 127. 7; (पृथिवीराज्यम् अर्हो ऽयं नाङ्गराज्यं नरेश्वरः) 1. 127 16; Karṇa is called the king of the Aṅgas in various contexts: (i) Śiśupāla calls Karṇa the chief of the Vaṅga and Aṅga countries (वङ्गाङ्ग-विषयाध्यक्ष) 2. 41. 9; (ii) Śalya refers to the rulership of Karṇa of the Aṅgas (अङ्गेषु … कर्ण येषाम् अधिपतिर् भवान्) 8. 30. 83; (3) While recounting the ex-ploits of Karṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentions Aṅgas (!) among the countries conquered by Karṇa and made to pay tribute (सुह्मान् अङ्गांश् च पुण्ड्रांश् च … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 19-20; (4) When Jayadratha was subdued by Karṇa in a wrestling bout, he (J.), pleased with Karṇa, gave him the city of Mālinī in the Aṅga country (प्रीत्या ददौ स कर्णाय मालिनीम् नगरीम् अथ । अङ्गेषु) 12. 5. 6; (5) Arjuna, during the period of exile, visited all the holy places in the Aṅga, Vaṅga and Kaliṅga countries (अङ्गवङ्ग-कलिङ्गेषु … जगाम तानि सर्वाणि तीर्थान्य् आयतनानि च) 1. 207. 9; (6) Aṅga country mentioned among those which were con-quered by Sahadeva before the Rājasūya (यः काशीन् अङ्गमगधान् … युधाजयत्) 5. 49. 28 (however, according to 2. 27. 16-18 it was Bhīma who subjugated Karṇa; in 2. 28 where Sahadeva's expedition is described there is no reference to the Aṅga country); (7) The Kṣatriyas of the Aṅga and Vaṅga countries mentioned among those who brought riches by hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (अङ्गा वङ्गाश् च पुण्ड्राश् च … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शत-शः) 2. 48. 15-16; (8) Aṅgas and Vaṅgas mentioned among those people who along with their kings were present at the Rāja-sūya of Yudhiṣṭhira and served meals (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालान् … सवङ्गाङ्गान् … आगतान् अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 22; (9) The army of the easterners protected by the ruler of the Aṅga country and by Kṛpa marched out for the battle (तद् अङ्गपतिना गुप्तं कृपेण च॥।प्रा-च्यानाम् अभवद् बलम्) 6. 17. 28; (10) When Ayutāyus and Dīrghāyus, the sons of Śrutāyus and Acyutāyus, were killed by Arjuna, the Aṅga warriors, riding elephants, attacked Arjuna (अङ्गास् तु गजवारेण पाण्डवं पर्यवारयन् । … हस्तिसादिनः) 7. 68. 31; (11) When Arjuna attacked the army of the Saṃśaptakas (8. 12. 54), the Aṅga warriors, riding elephants, along with Kaliṅga, Vaṅga, and Niṣāda warriors attacked him (कलिङ्गवङ्गाङ्गनिषादवीरा जिघांसवः पाण्डवम् अभ्यधावन्) 8. 12. 59; (12) The Aṅga warriors, along with Vaṅgas and others, riding elephants and skilled in fighting with elephants, attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna (हस्तिभिस् तु महा-मात्राः … धृष्टद्युम्नं जिघांसन्तः क्रुद्धाः पार्षतम् अभ्ययुः ॥ … गजयो-धिनः । अङ्गा वङ्गाश् च … गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 1-3; (13) Sahadeva, after killing the elephant of a Punḍra warrior, attacked the elephant of an Aṅga warrior; Nakula took on himself the fight with the Aṅga warrior and his elephant; the Aṅga warrior threw तोमरस् on Nakula; the warrior (here called म्लेच्छ and Ācārya-पुत्र) fell down along with his elephant; at the death of this Aṅga warrior, other warriors from the Aṅga country with their elephants attacked Nakula (विवर्मध्वज-जीवितम् । तं कृत्वा द्विरदं भूयः सह-देवो ऽङ्गम् अभ्यगात् ॥ सहदेवं तु नकुलो वारयित्वाङ्गम् आर्दयत् । … अङ्गश् चिक्षेप तोमरान् । स पपात हतो म्लेच्छस् तेनैव सह दन्तिना ॥ आचार्यपुत्रे निहते … अङ्गाः क्रुद्धा महामात्रा नागैर् नकुलम् अभ्य-युः) 8. 17. 13-18; (14) Elephants from Kaliṅga, Vaṅga, Aṅga, Niṣāda and Ma-gadha countries along with their warriors mentioned among those who were killed by Bhīma (कलिङ्गवङ्गाङ्गनिषादमागधान् सदामदान् … निहन्ति यः शत्रुगणान् अने-कशः) 8. 49. 79; (15) Dhṛtarāṣṭra while recounting Kṛṣṇa's exploits mentioned Aṅgas, Vaṅgas and Kaliṅgas among the countries which were conquered by him in battle (अङ्गान् वङ्गान् कलिङ्गांश् च  … अजयद् रणे) 7. 10. 15 (this incident is not mentioned in the epic). F. Past events: (1) Lomapāda, a friend of Daśa-ratha, was the king of the Aṅgas (लोम-पाद इति ख्यातो अङ्गानाम् ईश्वरो ऽभवत्) 3. 110. 19; he, the king of the Aṅga country, called his ministers and consulted with them about the means to bring Ṛśyaśṛṅga to the Aṅga country; he asked the courte-zans to get Ṛśyaśṛṅga from his आश्रम to his country by some means (ततो ऽङ्ग-पतिर् आहूय सचिवान् … । यत्नम् अकरोन् मन्त्रणिश्चये॥।ऋश्यशृङ्गम् … आनयध्वम् विषयं मम शोभनाः ॥ ) 3. 110. 28, 31;
